introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).
Q6(ii)(b) : le graphique est a tracer par le candidat ; le corrige decrit l'echelle et les points. Q6(ii)(a) : les valeurs imprimees 1.7 et -1.7 sont des arrondis a 1 decimale de racine de 3.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) Solve for $\theta$, in the range $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$, the equation $\sin2\theta-\cos\theta=0$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$:

$2\sin\theta\cos\theta-\cos\theta=0\ \Rightarrow\ \cos\theta\,(2\sin\theta-1)=0.$

- $\cos\theta=0$: $\theta=90^\circ$ or $270^\circ$.
- $\sin\theta=\dfrac12$: $\theta=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$.

(Do not divide by $\cos\theta$: that would lose the solutions $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$.)

**$\theta=30^\circ,\ 90^\circ,\ 150^\circ,\ 270^\circ$.**

Evaluate $f(x)=\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x$ at the missing values (it helps to note that $f(x)=2\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$):

- $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$: $\sqrt3\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+\dfrac12=\dfrac32+\dfrac12=2$.
- $x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$: $\sqrt3\cdot\left(-\dfrac12\right)+\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=0$.
- $x=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$: $\sqrt3\cdot\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)-\dfrac12=-\dfrac32-\dfrac12=-2$.
- $x=\dfrac{11\pi}{6}$: $\sqrt3\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\dfrac12=\dfrac32-\dfrac12=1$.

Completed table (the printed values $\pm1.7$ are $\pm\sqrt3$ to 1 d.p.):

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ | $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ | $\pi$ | $\frac{7\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{3\pi}{2}$ | $\frac{5\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{11\pi}{6}$ | $2\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | 1.7 | **2** | 1.7 | 1 | **0** | -1 | -1.7 | **-2** | -1.7 | -1 | 0 | **1** | 1.7 |

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Taking 1 cm to represent $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ radian units on the $x$-axis and 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Scales: on the $x$-axis $0$ to $2\pi$ is $12$ cm (each $\frac{\pi}{6}$ is 1 cm); on the $y$-axis from $-2$ to $2$ is $8$ cm.

Plot the 13 points from the table, for example $(0,\,1.7)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\,2\right)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{3},\,1.7\right)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\,1\right)$, $\left(\frac{2\pi}{3},\,0\right)$, $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},\,-1\right)$, $\left(\pi,\,-1.7\right)$, $\left(\frac{7\pi}{6},\,-2\right)$, $\left(\frac{4\pi}{3},\,-1.7\right)$, $\left(\frac{3\pi}{2},\,-1\right)$, $\left(\frac{5\pi}{3},\,0\right)$, $\left(\frac{11\pi}{6},\,1\right)$, $\left(2\pi,\,1.7\right)$.

Join them with a smooth curve: it is a sine-type wave of amplitude $2$, maximum $2$ at $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$, minimum $-2$ at $x=\frac{7\pi}{6}$, crossing the $x$-axis at $x=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi}{3}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) From the graph or otherwise, write down the maximum value of $f(x)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the graph the highest point is at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ where $f(x)=2$. Algebraically, $f(x)=2\cos\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ has amplitude $2$.

**Maximum value of $f(x)=2$.**
